title: Conversation protocol mapper and eventized response shaper for OpenAI Chat compatibility
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement a compatibility layer that maps incoming OpenAI Chat Completions style requests into Redwood's internal conversation model and shapes outgoing responses/events to match OpenAI semantics. This ticket focuses on three hard problems: streaming deltas -> Redwood streaming events, function/tool call lifecycle mapping (initiate, partial tool output, final tool_result), and structured output enforcement (JSON schemas / object responses) while preserving observability and SLOs. The mapper must be toggleable (compat mode) and support both permissive passthrough and strict validation modes.
design_rationale: We chose an eventized approach so both streaming and non-streaming clients get a single predictable set of events: message.delta, message.function_call.start, message.function_call.chunk, message.function_call.end, and message.finish
Prefer preserving original OpenAI fields (role, name, function_call metadata) in emitted events to help downstream customers migrate with minimal changes

Trade-off: strict schema validation reduces mis-interpretation but increases latency and failure surface. We'll make strict validation opt-in per route and provide a permissive default with post-hoc eval alerts.
tasks: Define canonical event envelope and wire format for OpenAI compatibility (spec in Confluence)
Implement request translator: map OpenAI messages, system prompts, temperature/stop tokens into Redwood request model
Implement response shaper for streaming: transform Redwood token streams into OpenAI-style delta chunks and event markers
Function calling lifecycle: detect function_call hints, route to local function runner / tool adapter, stream partial results back as function_call.chunk events
Structured output enforcement: integrate existing schema validator and add graceful fallback hooks
Instrumentation: add metrics for conversion latency, dropped tokens, tool-call error rates, and compatibility-mode rollouts
End-to-end tests: unit + integration with simulated OpenAI clients, tool runners, and load test for streaming SLOs
Create migration guide and sample SDK snippets (Node/Python) showing compat headers and opt-in flags
acceptance_criteria: Incoming OpenAI Chat request with streaming=true produces a sequence of events that an OpenAI client can consume without modification
Tool/function call sequences produce start/chunk/end events in the correct order and deliver final function_result as JSON content when available
Structured JSON outputs validated against provided schema when strict mode enabled; invalid outputs trigger a clear error event and optional fallback
No more than 5ms median per-request translation overhead at 95th percentile under normal load (measured on dedicated test pool)
Verified with integration tests: Node 18 OpenAI SDK and Python openai client correctly receive streaming deltas and function call events using compat mode
Docs and migration guide published; console flag to enable compat mode per route
notes: Early spike showed difficulty reconciling OpenAI's function_call partials when tools emit streaming binary blobs. We will normalize tool outputs to base64-encoded chunk events with length metadata.

There is a subtle ordering issue when a model emits a token that triggers a function_call mid-stream. Plan: buffer until we see explicit function_call.start then flush prior tokens as a 'prelude' chunk to the client.
We should reuse the existing streaming backpressure hooks in the runtime to avoid head-of-line blocking when mapping to OpenAI streaming frames. Marcus to pair with runtime team.
Security: because function_call arguments can contain PII, compat layer must honor request-level KMS/HSM policies and redact tokens from logs per policy. See security checklist.
comments: 2025-02-13 Ava Chen: Spiked a PoC that translates a simple 3-message OpenAI conversation into Redwood request format. Found that stop token handling needs special case because Redwood accepts multiple stop sequences. Filed task to canonicalize stops.

2025-02-20 Marcus Rivera: Implemented initial streaming shaper; pushes delta tokens as 'message.delta' but currently loses function_call.name metadata on chunk boundaries. Investigating adding a header on each chunk with active function_call id.

2025-02-24 Priya Patel (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria and clarified rollout: compat mode should be off by default for enterprise customers; enable via console feature flag and per-route override. Added to tasks.

2025-02-26 Sofia Martinez (Design): Suggested a minimal event envelope to preserve backwards compatibility with the widest set of clients. Shared a sample client-side snippet that expects 'event: message.delta' lines.

2025-02-28 Marcus Rivera: Created draft PR #12345 with translator and tests. CI failing on an integration test that simulates a long-running tool call (tool streaming + abort). Reproduced locally. Workaround: propagate client abort upstream to tool runner and emit a function_call.end with status 'aborted'.

2025-03-03 Oliver Grant (Security): Security review: flagged logging of raw function args. Action: implement per-route redact_rules and mask before persisting events. Marking security_review_required=true.
2025-03-04 Marcus Rivera: Updated PR with redact rules and added a simulation that validates strict schema mode rejects malformed JSON structures and emits an error event. Ready for eng-review.
